brief_text: a ball rolls down a ramp and comes to rest in a cup

usage.text:
The ramp is a 10° tilted box whose lower end sits just above the near wall of an open box cup. The ball starts at rest near the top and gravity rolls it down. It leaves the ramp at about 0.8 m/s, drops roughly 13 cm and lands about 12 cm inside the cup. Rolling friction on the ball (`condim="6"`, rolling coefficient 0.002) and impacts with the cup walls should bring it under 5 cm/s well before 6 s. These figures are hand calculations; I haven't run the simulation.

verdict.what_happens: The ball rolls down the ramp from rest under gravity, leaves the ramp's end at about 0.9 m/s, drops over the near wall onto the cup bottom, bounces lightly off the far wall, and settles inside the cup by about 2 s. It creeps only a few centimetres over the remaining time and finishes at rest on the cup bottom at x ≈ 0.29 m.

usage.text:
The ball starts at rest near the top of the ramp and gravity rolls it down, accelerating to about 0.7 m/s. At 0.97 s it leaves the ramp's end at about 0.9 m/s, clears the cup's near wall and lands on the cup bottom at 1.12 s. It rolls across to the far wall and hits it at 1.42 s, briefly hopping off the bottom. It rebounds slowly and counts as at rest by 1.98 s at x ≈ 0.32, well inside the cup. After that it creeps back very slowly, about 3 cm over 4 s, much less than the 5 cm/s threshold. It ends at (0.29, 0, 0.04), resting on the cup bottom.
